RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Bettered low-key debut when second at Newcastle (7f, AW) in December, despite racing too freely; makes turf debut after 225-day break but the drop in trip could be a good move; big player if fully tuned up.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Slightly disappointing when dropped to 5f for latest run and remains unproven on ground quicker than good, but was placed twice over 6f beforehand (maiden/handicap) and can play a major role if aided by first-time blinkers.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Boasts the best form in this line-up, having twice finished second (once over C&D) on fast ground in the spring, but seems to have lost his way since; beaten over 18l when last of four at Ripon (6f, good) a fortnight ago and arrives here with questions to answer.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well beaten on both outings, the latest here (7f, good) on seasonal/stable debut in June; drops back to 6f with hood added today.

Spotlight: Third at Beverley (7.4f, good) and justified favouritism in a five-runner novice at Ayr (7f, good to firm) four weeks later, outpaced over 2f out but rallying strongly; the fourth from that Ayr race is the only one to have run since and he won; while 1m might have made more appeal, this one clearly looks capable of better.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: Spg Property, Alfa Site & Graeme Curnow

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Favourite both starts, when unable to hold off a strong finisher at Leicester (7f, good) and unable to threaten at Chester (6f, good; third at 11-10); the winner on first occasion took the Group 2 Vintage at Goodwood this week for his second win since, and the third also won next time; moving back up to 7f should help this one on nursery debut.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: All three races were over 7f on good ground, best on second occasion when third of seven at Sandown despite having traffic issues and stumbling; raced up with pace, but faded, when favourite there last time; goes handicapping and his earlier promise can't be forgotten.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Modest form on first two starts (6f, AW/good) and stiff task when well beaten on soft ground for latest; gelded since; bred to stay 1m/1m2f in time and needs a market check on this handicap debut.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 16,000gns yearling and half-sister to a 6f winner; 18-1 at Epsom (7f, good to firm) but beaten only 2l after starting slowly; should be wiser this time and have every chance.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 5,000gns yearling; 13th foal; half-sister to five winners including Staxton (6f; RPR 106), Lazarus Bell (7f 2yo; 89), Classic Pursuit (prolific 5f/6f; 89) and Satin Snake (7f; 81); dam 1m4f winner (80); rare 2yo runner for the yard.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 10,000euros 2yo; second foal; dam 1m-1m4f winner (RPR 87), closely related to winners Green Storm (Group-placed 1m1f 2yo) and Bulldog Spirit (1m-1m6f); trainer has sent out ten 2yo winners on turf this season.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 5,000gns foal; seventh foal; half-sister to 7f winner One Night Thunder (RPR 93); dam 6f AW winner (91), out of 1m4f/2m winning sister to Group 2 winners Nearly Caught (1m7f) and Pale Mimosa (2m); the market should be informative.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to 6f/7f winner Eye Of Dubai (RPR 97); dam French 7.5f-1m2f winner, half-sister to German 1m3f winner Sokol; makes sense to check the betting.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 8,000gns yearling; half-sister to 5f winner Beerwah (RPR 70); dam placed 5f-1m (102), sister to 7f winner Jalaad; stable's newcomers are usually best watched.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Low-level form thus far (over 5f) and likely to fare better when handicapping.

Twice runner-up before winning a 7f AW maiden in October and then gelded; finished last of the four when favourite for his handicap debut at Catterick (7f, good to firm) but he raced freely up front and didn't look at home on the track; worth another chance.

OwnerName: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
Spotlight: 7f maiden winner in May and held his own in handicaps until a poor last run, since when he's been gelded; entitled to play a part if back to best.

Newmarket maiden winner for Harry Charlton last August (6f, good to firm); subsequently sold for 90,000gns; building momentum in handicaps for his new yard, last time holding every chance over C&D and going down by a length; solid prospects off 1lb lower.

Goodwood novice winner in May of last year; 0-9 in the meantime and progress has levelled out; ran no more than okay when third of five in a new tongue-tie last week at Lingfield (6f, good to firm); swaps cheekpieces for first-time blinkers here.

Started off well for Ruth Carr, although did appear to throw away (hung right) a winning opportunity when runner-up at Carlisle (7f, good) in May; better than bare facts - denied a clear run - when sixth of nine at Thirsk latest; fairly treated, so isn't discounted.

14-race maiden; forced to switch right - circumnavigated the field - when third of 11 at Ripon (6f, good; 11-4 favourite) a fortnight ago; worth another go over 7f (first since debut) as he seeks to make the breakthrough; likely player.

Overcame slow start to win in newly applied visor at Leicester (7f; from 3lb lower) on penultimate start; less productive (fourth of five) back there over 6f subsequently; cheekpieces refitted, and Christian Howarth's 3lb claim can assist.

Modest in maidens, the pick of her three starts coming on Catterick debut (7f, soft; fourth, beaten nearly 7l) last July; has been given a nine-week break since low-key Chester comeback; hood applied for handicap debut.

Made the most of a favourable draw, running down the pacesetter at Redcar (6f, good; from 4lb lower) in June; below that level at Thirsk, but this is easier, and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim is handy; stamina is untested beyond 6f.

1-12; placed over C&D in April, and gave it a good go from the front when third to Vega's Virtue at Ripon (1m, good) a fortnight ago; sports newly applied cheekpieces seeking that extra edge with the drop back to 7f in her favour; chance.

Sole win from 24 starts came at Brighton (7f, good; from 9lb higher) in May 2024; generally disappointing for this trainer, weakening on first start since wind surgery at Ffos Las (7.5f, good; beaten over 7l) 32 days ago; 3lb lower.

0-4; failed to take step forward on Ripon handicap debut (6f; seventh of nine, 28-1; always towards rear); still early days but, equally, there's little to suggest that she can play a role in the finish.

Eight-race maiden; has plummeted in the weights since sent handicapping (down 16lb); weakened quickly when last of eight in first-time cheekpieces at Wetherby (5.5f) latest; difficult to identify many positives; headgear tweaked.

Ran well (third) on Southwell debut (5f maiden; 33-1) last April, but it's been all downhill since, beating only a single rival in two AW starts this year; cheekpieces discarded off 95-day break for turf return; monitor only.

0-8; no match for Act Of Violence at Ripon (6f, good; 10-1) a fortnight ago, but that was a step back in the right direction, and third-placed Get Up Everybody puts that form to the test in the first division (4:50); key player on first attempt at 7f (dam a 7f-8.4f winner).

2-5 over C&D; scrambled home to justify favouritism from Operation Gimcrack (runs in first division) in this last year; placed numerous times since, including at Yarmouth (7f; 10-1) on penultimate start; slow start scuppered chance latest.

Modest since joining Nigel Tinkler (0-6) but there was merit to his Carlisle second (7f, soft) on penultimate start; that track seems to bring out the best of his abilities so, although fairly weighted, he couldn't rate as a confident pick.

0-7; respectable comeback at Nottingham (5f, good; fourth, beaten 3l) in May, but hasn't built on that, including in blinkers (discarded) the last twice; tough to say how he'll fare on first go at 7f; safer options elsewhere.

Five-race maiden; lost shoe when failing to figure (11 of 14) on handicap debut at Bath (1m; 25-1) seven weeks ago; 2lb lower in the right type of race, but with clear improvement required to threaten.

Finished strongly to resume winning ways over C&D (good to soft; from 2lb lower) in May; hasn't operated at the same level since, but overall strike rate (10-80) is admirable for the level; forecast ground perhaps faster than ideal.

Seven-race maiden; in rear throughout in newly applied headgear combination (discarded) over 6f here five weeks ago; eased another 3lb in the handicap since, so isn't written off yet; prudent to consult the market.
27-race maiden; placed in this same headgear combination at Wolverhampton and Chester (both 7f) before producing poor performance at Chester latest; opposed on the balance of probability.
Yet to win on turf (0-12); hasn't managed to beat many rivals in three starts this year, only eighth of nine at Catterick (7f; 28-1) 24 days ago; handicap mark continues to slide.

Won the Legends Classified Stakes here (1m; 40-1) last September; knocking on the door over 7f here (23) in recent times; competitively weighted from an unchanged mark, and a danger to all if allowed uncontested lead back at 6f.

C&D winner; runner-up on last two starts, beaten a nose at Carlisle (6f, good; 5-2 favourite) four weeks ago; that form looks solid, with the winner running well in a Class 4 at York subsequently; 1lb higher, but does have Alex Jary's 3lb claim to assist; key player.

No turf win since July 2023; ran respectably (fifth) on stable debut at Yarmouth (7f, good) in May and has had excuses since, including when stumbling and unseating his rider at the start at Goodwood on Wednesday; 3lb below last winning mark (AW), and with a 5lb claimer booked.

Lightly raced filly who is continuing to make progress; runner-up on her last two starts, latest when a neck behind Saucy Jane on handicap debut at Thirsk (6f; good to firm; 20-1); 1lb higher in a slightly more competitive contest but can't be ruled out.

Ripon specialist (ten wins at that track); run down only by Reigning Profit and Rock Of England when attempting to win the race named in his honour there (5f) 26 days ago; no issue with this return to 6f and has been placed here previously.

1-21; close fourth at Thirsk (6f, good; from 7lb higher) in April; has lost his way since, failing to beat many in 5f contests at Pontefract, Beverley, and Chester; questions to be answered for the time being.

Made the breakthrough, justifying favouritism at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) 17 days ago; while she has responded to the removal of the hood, this represents a step back up the ladder (Class 5) from a 4lb higher mark; her task isn't an insurmountable one, though.

Promising sort last autumn, winning a maiden and second in a novice hurdle; however, he has to rebound in a major way from two pulled-up runs.

Spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt in point-to-points at Loughrea in May; bought for E35,000 at Tattersalls later that month; probably best watched on Rules' debut; tongue tied.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Belied odds of 66-1 to run a huge race on debut at Roscommon when she had a few of these behind; enters calculations now with improvement likely to be forthcoming.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Okay effort when fourth at Tramore on debut; didn't build on that when tailed off at Cork latest; others preferred.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Best effort yet when finishing ahead of Aodha's Arrow and Back In Favour at Roscommon on latest; should strip fitter for that run and holds an each way chance.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Harzand filly; half-sister to winners Phantom Gold (bumper/2m4f hurdle) and Parisian Fashion (2m4f hurdle); dam useful bumper and 2m/2m1f hurdle winner; makes some appeal on paper and worth checking in the market; tongue tied.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Modest enough efforts in bumpers at Leopardstown when beaten 16l into fourth and at Limerick when beaten 32l into fifth; new cheekpieces need to eke out more.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Displayed potential on debut at Limerick (2m, soft) two months ago, outpaced but keeping on for a 9.75l third of 9; should come on for that and now sports a tongue tie; not discounted for place purposes.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Old Persian filly; half-sister to winners Miami Present (useful 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase) and Florida Calling (point); dam German 7f/7.5f winner, half-sister to 1m Listed Flat and useful 2m-2m2f hurdle/chase winner Moon Over Miami; market can guide on debut.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: 25-1 and beaten 25l on debut at Tramore in May; others make more appeal.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: 40-1 but creditable effort on debut at Killarney last month, showing up well before fading in the final furlong into a 6.5l third of 15; likely to improve for that run and outside place claims.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Heavy defeats at big odds in bumpers at Roscommon and Wexford; seems safe to rule out.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Promise in all three starts; beaten similar distances when fifth on debut at Cork and again on second start at Wexford; didn't get a clear run when beaten 3.5l into fourth at Sligo on latest; can give another good account.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
OwnerName: Going For The One Syndicate/Michael McEvoy/Jimmy Whittle
Spotlight: Was bang there when falling at the last in sole point-to-point start at Lisronagh in April; bumper winners in pedigree and yard had a bumper winner at Ballinrobe last month; market can guide on Rules' debut.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Poet's Word mare; dam bumper/2m hurdle winner, sister to smart bumper and 2m2f-2m6f hurdle winner Glens Melody, closely related to useful 2m-3m hurdle winner Lean Araig, out of 2m Flat, bumper and useful 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase winner; lots of appeal on paper and top yard has won five of last six renewals.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Brother to 6f Group 2 2yo winner Beautify; was the stable second-string on debut when runner-up in what is traditionally a strong Curragh maiden; that was 7f but looked as if he would stay this trip; looks the one to beat on that run.

A 75,000gns breeze-up purchase in April and from a middle-distance family; recovered from a slow start to run well on debut at Killarney over this trip; can be more competitive with that experience behind him.

First foal; dam twice-raced half-sister to winners Alluringly (9.4f Listed) and Toogood Tobetrue (useful 6f 2yo), from the family of Derby winners and oustanding sires Galileo and Sea The Stars; E300,000 yearling is the stable second-string on debut but is still respected.

Fifth foal; half-brother to winners Pinot Gris (10.3f/1m5f Flat, RPR 87; useful 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase) and Postdamerstrasse (Italian 7.5f); dam 1m4f/12.5f winner (85); E18,000 foal made E40,000 as a yearling; by a promising first-crop sire and related to winners so could run respectably.

Glimmers of ability in three runs last season for John Kiely; caught the eye of the stewards when a never nearer sixth on final start for that stable here over 7f in October (heavy); worth a market check on first run for new yard.

Betrayed inexperience when a 3.25l sixth of 15 in a Curragh maiden on debut in May (1m2f, good); should improve plenty for that run and the choice of Foley but whether this drop back in trip will suit is debateable and drawn wide.
Has displayed winning potential when fourth in maidens at Dundalk in December (7f) and at Gowran (1m, soft) in April; off 114 days but clearly has ability, is well drawn and market can guide.

Rated 74; promise in maidens last year (including here over 7f on soft) and in first two runs this term at Leopardstown; no impact behind Gliondar in 1m Curragh maiden on good latest; could do better back on softer ground in first-time blinkers.
Caught the eye when a 6.25l third of 16 on debut at Gowran; had excuses when sixth on latest at Naas (scoped dirty); tricky draw here and Foley prefers Royal Bones.
33-1 and beaten 20l on debut in fillies' maiden at Gowran; may need more time.
Minor promise over 7f at Fairyhouse on debut and built on that when a 1l third of 7 upped to 10.5f (good) at Down Royal at 80-1; place claims dropped back in trip.
Well beaten in barrier trial; modest efforts in maidens at Navan and Gowran; will get a handicap mark after this.

OwnerName: Sheikh Khalid Bin Ali Al Khalifa
Spotlight: Make Believe gelding; brother to 1m AW winner Suspicion (RPR 85); dam unraced half-sister to winners Ninjago (6f Listed) and Florestans Match (6f), out of French 7.5f Listed winner; likely best watched on debut.
Huge odds for all three starts and slowly away in two of them; hard to make a case for on form.
80-1 and failed to beat a rival on debut at Gowran; hard to fancy
Modest maiden rated just 30; impossible to fancy in a race of this nature.

Gained second career win off just 1lb higher at Down Royal in May (7f, good); lost form since and was soundly beaten behind a couple of these rivals over 8.5f here on Tuesday; would prefer a sounder surface.

British raider seeking a hat-trick after back to back fast ground wins over 7.5f at Beverley; has gone up 8lb for those two victories; clearly in fine fettle and nicely drawn but may need quicker ground.
Had been running well before a below par effort at the Curragh last time over an inadequate 5f; runner up over C&D last year off 8lb higher; could bounce back.
Goes well at this venue and was only reeled in close to home over 8.5f here on Tuesday; runs off the same mark now and nicely drawn so can't discount dropped back in trip; obvious chance.
Two wins when trained in France over 6f and 1m1f; no impact in first two runs for this stable; mark sliding but drawn wide and others make more appeal.
Three-time winner but no joy since July 2023; mark sliding but hasn't looked like taking advantage in recent starts; beaten 10.5l when down the field at the Curragh on latest.

Has failed to add to his Gowran maiden win in April 2024 (7f, good); not a bad effort when a close fourth behind Minaun View in a Bellewstown claimer latest (Gloriously Glam second); handicap form unconvincing; new headgear combination tried.
Won twice last year and is now 2lb below his last success but heavy defeats both starts this term; blinkers go back on but they didn't do much for him when he wore them before.

Four-time winner claimed out of Ado McGuinness' yard for E10,000 after finishing a 0.5l second behind in form Minaun View in Bellewstown claimer; 8lb below last handicap win but difficult draw on first start for new stable.

Won this race last year off 4lb lower for Mick Mulvany; has run well on all three previous visits to this venue and should be sharper for her seasonal reappearance and stable debut at Ballinrobe 40 days ago; visor added to tongue tie; could go well.

Gained second turf win at Roscommon in May (10.5f, yielding) off 4lb lower; has come up short twice since off revised mark but ran well off 1lb higher at this meeting last year over 8.5f so not dismissed stepped up in trip in first-time blinkers.

Four-time winner landed this race last season off 72; was running off that mark when winning at Roscommon on latest (10.5f, good); 6lb rise makes things tougher but she's got a nice low draw, ground is fine and should be in the mix again.

Dual 1m winner in Britain, both on good ground; no show last year for this stable but both runs this year encouraging, only beaten 2.25l when fifth at Ayr latest (1m2f, good); not well drawn here, however, and may need quicker ground; visored.

5-26 on turf; just 2lb higher than when winning at Leopardstown in October (1m2f, heavy); beaten 3.75l into fifth in this race last season off this mark but hard to fancy on this season's efforts and others look better treated.

Seven-time turf winner on a hat-trick after back to back wins at Navan (1m2f, good) and Killarney (11.5f, good); has gone up 11lb for those wins but she has won off higher marks in the past; however, was unplaced in the 5.40 here on Thursday.
Maiden showed more than enough for Charlie Fellowes last season to suggest he could win races; below best when last seen at Newmarket in October; worth a market check on debut for Gordon Elliott.

Ex-French performer 4-12 on the AW but just 1-11 on turf for former yard; yet to show much since joining this stable but drops in grade and shrewd yard won nice pot here earlier this week; check the market.

Both Flat wins at this trip, a Curragh maiden on good in July 2024 and a Roscommon handicap (soft) off 6lb lower last October; has failed to fire on previous runs at this venue, including when beaten 19l over 16.5f here on Wednesday.

Both turf wins came over 1m but proved stamina for 1m4f when scoring at Dundalk in February; nice prep run for this at Navan over 1m2f and the step back up to this trip is a plus but he's got a tricky draw to overcome.

Enjoyed a purple patch in 2023, winning five times on the Flat (and once over hurdles) for Mick Mulvany; solid run over hurdles here on Wednesday; won over 8.5f at this meeting in 2023, this trip is within her range and she's 4lb below her last success; player.

British raider; won twice on the Flat when trained by Dermot Weld (1-9 on turf); ran well in a Market Rasen maiden hurdle on penultimate; out of depth in Listed hurdle here earlier this week; this more realistic but difficult draw.

Up 6lb for breakthrough Flat win at Roscommon in May (1m4f, yielding), beating subsequent winner Obscenity by 2.75l; soundly beaten in Punchestown maiden hurdle latest but has to be considered back on the level from low draw.

Hasn't won on the Flat since scoring over C&D at this meeting in 2023; went close at Navan in April (1m5f, gd-yld) off 2lb lower; hasn't backed that up since but did run a nice race over hurdles here on Wednesday.
Best on AW (6-12) but just 1-20 on turf; scored at Dundalk in March but soundly beaten back on turf the last twice (7l behind Thatwilldoso on penultimate); drawn wide; others more convincing.

Two-time 1m AW winner for former yard; went close on debut for this stable on last Flat start at Dundalk (10.5f); no impact over hurdles last thrice and 0-7 record on turf on the Flat doesn't inspire confidence; drawn wide.
French recruit; placed twice for former yard in 2025; 50-1 and never figured on return from 407 days off on stable debut at Ballinrobe 12 days ago; drawn wide and probably best watched for now.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 0-6 in handicaps, with regular progress/promise but not when favourite last time at Royal Ascot where he raced freely early on and ran out of steam after challenging over 2f out (finished 8l sixth of 17); it's much too early to forget his reappearance promise (also 1m4f on good to firm) but that latest run also casts some doubt on the suitability of this new trip.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 1m4f festival wins off much lower marks at Chester and Epsom last July when trained by the Moores; returned to Flat with an eye-catching effort at Royal Ascot (2m4f, good to firm; 12-1) last month, turning for home towards rear but running on into sixth of 20; back down in trip but one to note.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Close third in this last year and a creditable, running-on fourth of 16 at Royal Ascot (1m6f, good to firm) latest start; strong each-way chance.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: The future looked bright when he won the Melrose at York (1m6f, good to firm) last August but he's not built on that significantly; well held back in Britain for two Group races this May when last seen; off 12lb higher than in the Melrose, this return to a handicap may also be tough.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Stepped up to 1m6f with cheekpieces enlisted for last two starts and won them both, doing it smoothly at this track (good) and having to battle when prevailing by a neck in valuable race at Newmarket (good to firm); raised another 3lb but looks a serious contender once again.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Upset in the stalls when a disappointing favourite at this meeting last year (subsequently gelded); had a 1m6f win next time and solid performances when beaten about 3l on all three starts this season, sixth of 16 when back up to 1m6f at Royal Ascot latest; others saw it out better that day but he should have serious each-way claims.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won this race in 2024 before embarking on a long losing run; he's broken that with two 2m wins on the AW this year, most notably in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle last time; second in valuable race at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) in May was followed by a blip here; back up another 4lb since Newcastle but not entirely ruled out.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Not a prolific winner, with his waiting tactics, but he was fourth in the Ebor at York (1m6f, good to firm) last August off a 2lb higher mark; ran creditably on reappearance, before neither start since panned out favourably; only ninth in this last year on his only run at Goodwood.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: J William Rowley & S P C Woods
Spotlight: Won five-runner race here (upped to 2m, good) in May and made most when fifth of 20 in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle (2m, AW); no room over 1f out at Newbury two weeks ago but the speed with which he dropped out when jockey gave up was still rather disconcerting; place chance if bouncing back.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2-5 in France and also scored in December in Bahrain for new connections; fourth of eight at Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago was probably his best form but better is needed and he didn't settle well enough behind horses that day, so is seemingly not crying out for this longer trip.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2023 Royal Ascot winner who has also tasted the high life in top hurdle races; his attentions have been turned back to the Flat this year and he hasn't been in peak form; falling in the weights but still needs a revival; good 5lb claimer is enlisted.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Contested three Group races last summer; it's been 1m4f handicaps (good to firm) this season, registering his highest rating when fourth of eight at Newmarket in May but two disappointing shows at Ascot have followed; blinkered latest; stays at least 1m5f (unraced over this far) and he's 6lb lower than at Newmarket, but some caution is advised at present.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Two big runs over 1m4f here, including when third of nine in Listed race in May; not quite so good in two Ascot handicaps (1m6f/1m4f) since and there's a bit more to prove at this trip but that Listed run reads well.

OwnerName: T & Mrs L Standish & Mrs A Spence
Spotlight: He's run well on both visits to Goodwood, latest a close third in 1m2f Listed race here (good) in May after an absence, and the late headway he made when eighth in the Listed Wolferton at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) suggests this step up in trip could be a good move; each-way chance.

Lightly raced 4yo who won at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm) in May on his second start since being gelded and followed up in the Duke Of Edinburgh Handicap at Royal Ascot (1m4f, good to firm); he's by Frankel out of a Group 1 winner and could take this rise in grade in his stride; key player.

9yo who has won the last two runnings of this race (good to firm/good to soft) and has run well on both starts this season, most recently posting a cosy Listed win at Beverley (1m4f, good to firm); leading claims.

He was returning from a year off when down the field in the Wolferton at Royal Ascot in June, and may have needed that first run for Kevin Philippart De Foy; classy performer for Clive Cox prior to £2,000,000 sale, making the frame in several Group 1s, and can have a big say if back to his best.

Late headway once in the clear in the Listed Wolferton Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) in June, finishing seventh of 16, and outclassed in the Eclipse since (well beaten at 100-1); drops back in grade and the step back up in trip is worth a go, but he's 0-13 in Group/Listed races since winning the London Gold Cup in May 2024 and may again find a few too good.

Didn't really take to hurdling but she relished the step up in trip in this code when easily winning a 13-runner handicap at the Curragh (1m4f, good) in June; she has to prove that brilliance was no one-off but it was certainly an impressive performance and she could have a part to play today.

Ex-French 4yo who won Group 3 at Saint-Cloud (10.5f, good) last May; respectable Listed efforts on last two starts (including C&D) but hasn't shown enough on those outings to suggest he'll be making an impact today.

Won Meydan handicap (9.5f, good) in March and ran well in defeat in Listed races on next two starts (including here over 1m2f); however, no match for Al Aasy in Listed race at Beverley (1m4f, good to firm) four weeks ago and others have more substance to their claims.

5l third to Waardah in this last year, before career best when second in the Melbourne Cup (2m); back to best European form when second in Group 3 at Fairyhouse (1m6f, good; unraced on firmer) this month but will probably have to settle for a place here if others show their best.

Duelled with Consent over 1m6f last year; progressive ways continued in May with a win at Newmarket (substandard 1m4f Group 2, good to firm) and close second in Group 1 at Longchamp (near 2m, soft); the Hardwicke back over 1m4f at Royal Ascot six weeks ago was a stiff task and she hung right in first-time cheekpieces on her way to a heavy defeat; much more interesting today with no headgear and back up in trip.

Won twice here (soft/good to soft) last summer, latterly when leading over 2f out in this race and seeing off Danielle's challenge by three-quarters of a length; ran moderately on final 3yo start but reappearance this May was positive when second to a class act in Group 3 at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm); big player if back to her peak.

Pipped by Santorini Star in Group 2 at Doncaster (14.5f, good to soft) in September but turned the tables on her in fine style in Group 1 at Longchamp (1m6f, soft) in October; cut out tamely in the final 2f of another French Group 1 (near 2m, soft) on return but ten weeks have passed; never having raced on firmer than good asks quite a question but tough to beat if back to her best.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Reappeared with 2l win in the Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good); soundly beaten when favourite for the Oaks itself on testing ground at Epsom and put firmly in her place when fifth in Irish Oaks at the Curragh (1m4f, good to firm; 5-1); wore a hood and blinkers on first two starts this season, just cheekpieces on latest; some limitations have seemingly been exposed and others saw the race out better in her two Oaks bids.

Second to Waardah in this last year and fourth to Santorini Star and Consent in Group 2 at Doncaster (14.5f, good to soft) last September; routed her rivals in Listed event (1m2f, heavy) in November and reappeared with Group 3 win at York (1m6f, good; made most at 1-2) ten weeks ago; unraced on good to firm since 2024 (comfortably held); serious player if the ground is okay.

Chased home Far Above Dream, beaten a neck with the pair clear, in a C&D handicap in May; again finished behind that rival in the Wokingham six weeks ago (cheekpieces first time) and needs more to win but that is not out of the question.

Looked one to follow when bolting up at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in December; had numerous excuses for a series of subsequent defeats but things finally clicked again at York (6f, good to firm) last week, gamely repelling 20 rivals; 2lb wrong under his penalty but he has Group-race aspirations and shouldn't be passed over lightly.

He hasn't had a great deal of racing since July 2024 but, two wind surgeries and a gelding operation later, he has shown he retains a good chunk of his former ability (Group 2 winner at best) this year, in a tongue-tie on last two starts; finished just behind Soldier's Tree when fifth in the Wokingham (6f, good to firm) but was in front of that rival in a Group 3 at Newbury two weeks ago; 3lb well in and has the ability to feature but his tendency to forfeit ground at the start isn't ideal in a race of this depth.

Finished eighth behind Two Tribes in this race 12 months ago when 4lb lower; he is a better horse now, as emphasised by two 6f AW wins in January and a fine second in the Wokingham (cheekpieces first time) but he finished behind Two Tribes at Ascot last week and others look more appealing for win purposes.

OwnerName: L Bond & Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi
Spotlight: Has a history of running well at this meeting and Tuesday's fourth (5f, good) was another solid effort; this looks a much stiffer test though.

Another success story for James Owen, progressing well in 2025 and continuing the good work this time around with wins over C&D and at Newbury (both good ground); another step forward when fourth in the Wokingham, an effort that can be upgraded, and he races off the same mark today; 3-3 over C&D and sure to be popular.

Climbed the ranks as a 4yo, ending that campaign with placed efforts in the Ayr Silver Cup and at Ascot; down the field on seasonal return but he hasn't looked back since, winning at Epsom (6f, soft) on Derby day for the second year in succession, doing best of the low numbers in the Wokingham (the others in his group have done well since) and then seeing off 19 rivals at the Curragh (6.3f, good to firm) two weeks ago; showed a fantastic attitude on that latest occasion and his 6lb penalty shouldn't prevent another big performance.

Impressed at Windsor (6f, good to firm) in June; had an excuse at Ascot next time and spent the first half of the race in the unfavoured stands' side group when down the field there last week; this looks too demanding all the same.
Still has low mileage and is proven over C&D but he has come up well short in deep races since winning here last August; hood left off this time; others look safer.

Would have finished closer than tenth in the Wokingham at Royal Ascot (6f) granted a clear run; scaled new heights when beating his 14 rivals there (5f, also good to firm) three weeks ago, finishing his race off strongly; 3lb wrong under his penalty today and while he has more good races in him, this one might prove too demanding.

Having edged down the weights he offered a good deal more when third to Tuco Salamanca at Newcastle (6f, AW) in June; finished with a flourish when seventh behind Dubai Bling at Ascot (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago, a run that confirmed he was still in good order; returning to 6f will help and he can't be dismissed, for all that he has been well beaten in this race twice before (2022 and 2025).

He didn't make his debut until December but this 5yo is quickly making up for lost time, finishing third in a Listed race at Salisbury (6f, good) on his stable debut and then running a huge race in the Wokingham at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm), beaten just over one length into third off a 1lb lower mark; again raced freely when third in a Group 3 at Newbury (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago; still has potential after just six starts.

Beat his 21 rivals at York in May and added a handicap at Chester (6f, good) last month; ran a fine race behind Sondad at the Curragh two weeks ago and is 7lb better off for half a length this time; officially the best handicapped horse in the race (5lb ahead of his mark) and another big run should be forthcoming.

Blessed with a potent turn of foot and he has been impressive in winning 6f AW handicaps at Kempton and Newcastle this year; a 3lb rise for the latter success five weeks ago doesn't handicap him out of things and he ran well in his one visit to Goodwood; one to be interested in.

Finished fourth behind stablemate Two Tribes in this race 12 months ago when 8lb lower and enjoyed his finest hour when making most to win the Ayr Gold Cup (6f, soft) last September; successful in Dubai early in the year and although his results have been mixed since returning to Britain, he retains plenty of ability; down the field over 5f here on Tuesday when a change of tactics failed to bear fruit; better can be expected today.

Profile is hit and miss but conditions won't faze him; he looked good at Carlisle (6f, good to firm; cheekpieces first time) in May and brings relatively low mileage but he was only midfield in the Wokingham and is 1lb higher today, so needs a big personal best.

Made all up the stands' rail when springing a 40-1 surprise in this race in 2024; added another major handicap when dominating last year's Wokingham; failed to beat a rival in his next three starts though (including in this race) and he has been absent for 314 days; his draw gives him the chance to repeat the heroics of 2024 but this looks a tough assignment on his return.

Three front-running AW wins in the spring saw him soar up the handicap; he didn't run badly off his revised mark at Epsom on Derby day but it would be a surprise if he were up to a task of this magnitude.

Quickly established himself as a smart sprinter, winning Group 2 and Group 3 prizes at Meydan (both 5f; good to firm and good) in early 2025; the addition of cheekpieces saw him return to his best when second in a 5f Group 3 on Dundalk AW last October; not quite at his best in two runs in Dubai in January and absent since; new blinkers need to have a positive effect.

Won five of his ten starts for Richard Fahey, notably a local Group 3 in Qatar in November 2024; absent for 593 days and gelded prior to his stable debut at Pontefract (6f, good) last month, a race in which he was caught out wide but plugged on for second behind the thriving easy winner; clearly retains ability but this will demand much more.

On the up in 2025, completing a hat-trick before fine runs at Royal Ascot and in the Ayr Gold Cup (beaten favourite in this race in between); had a wind operation prior to reappearance but he has finished down the field in both starts since, the Wokingham on latest; down in the weights but a full revival is essential; tongue-tie experiment last time is quickly aborted.

Two wins in Dubai early in the year before coming up short in Group 1 company in March and June; back on the up with a 7f Listed win at Chester three weeks ago; this looks a tough task under 6lb penalty though.

OwnerName: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
Spotlight: He has done all his winning on AW but his fourth at Leicester (6f, good to firm) in April is a comparable standard; can win races on the grass but perhaps not this one.

6f winner at Thirsk (good) in May and back at a similar level when a keeping-on third behind Dubai Bling at Ascot (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago; should run his race but others are perhaps better treated.

Best known for his AW exploits but he is fine on turf and has a lower mark in this sphere; went desperately close at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) 15 days ago, a race in which the first two pulled clear in the closing stages from a subsequent winner; 2lb ahead of the handicapper and he was successful on his only visit to Goodwood; interesting.

His impressive Newmarket success last May saw him hit hard by the handicapper and he hasn't added to it; chasing home Sondad at Epsom (6f, soft) in June represented his best run of the year but he failed to build on it at Windsor last time; others look safer.

Surged to the front 1f out when dominant in this race (good to soft) 12 months ago; 7lb higher this time around but he was better than ever when second in a hot handicap at Ascot last week (7f, good to firm) when coming from further back than ideal; 2lb ahead of the handicapper and he has a fine chance of becoming the fifth horse to win back-to-back Stewards' Cups (Commanche Falls in 2021 and 2022 was the latest).

Campaigned over shorter this term, posting a useful AW win on reappearance and not disgraced at Newmarket most recently; showed respectable 7f form as a 2yo, including a good effort in the maiden on this card and a success at Chester; still fairly unexposed over this distance; interesting.

Versatile sort who held on narrowly from Proud Nation over 7f at Newmarket (good to firm) most recently, adding to his 2yo sprint wins and taking record to 3-7; ran creditably over C&D in May; solid chance.

Gelded since finishing last when favourite for the Britannia at Royal Ascot (1m); had progressive 7f form previously and recorded a wide-margin success at Newmarket (good) the time before, taking record over this trip to 2211; may still have more to offer and remains of interest.

Won on the nod at Doncaster (good to firm) last time, looking suited by the step up to 7f and surging back to form; unexposed over this trip and may remain competitive, provided he takes to first-time cheekpieces (faced difficult task when once in blinkers).

Prevailed narrowly in small field when upped to 7f at Newmarket (good to firm) last time, taking record to 2-4; goes into deeper waters but remains unexposed, particularly at this distance; wears first-time headgear.

Has form figures of 114, all at Chester (6f and around 7f), since being gelded (maiden previously); not disgraced last time but has something to prove off the same mark switched to a different venue and upped in grade.

Took a while to hit the target but he had some notable maiden form, including at this meeting last year, and now bids for a hat-trick after wins under Jack Nicholls at Pontefract (6f maiden, good to soft) and Catterick (7f handicap; good to firm); further improvement is possible; respected.

Broadly progressive gelding who has form figures of 11127 in turf handicaps, the latest effort best forgiven (met trouble); ran well in a competitive field over C&D the time before; still 9lb above last winning mark but Harry Vigors takes off a useful 5lb; in the mix.
Commenced career with a record of 221 on AW; far from solid on his Listed/Group form on turf since (peak effort may not be reliable) and has something to prove off his mark; gelded since last run.

The class angle in this field and has earned top weight on handicap debut, having ended his progressive 2yo season with good efforts in a Newmarket Group 2 (7f, good to firm) and Canadian Grade 1 (1m, firm); a likely danger provided he's back in similar form with Listed reappearance under his belt.

Low-mileage colt who registered his 2yo success in a York maiden and posted two sound efforts since handicapping, beaten narrowly by Ironwill at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) latest; may do better still; not ruled out.

Appears to have his limitations, being 2-2 in Class 5 but 0-5 in higher grades; gained the latest success at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) last week; opposed from 6lb out of the weights in this markedly better race.

Back in his comfort zone at Epsom (7f, good) last time, taking Class 4 record to 3-3; sold out of George Boughey's yard for 28,000gns since; returns to deeper waters off a demanding mark; new headgear.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: Thrice-raced colt who is moving steadily in the right direction, third at Newbury (7f, good to firm) most recently; however, likely needs further progress to open his account in this field and he's the stable second string on jockey arrangements.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: 450,000gns breeze-up 2yo purchase who appeared to run well, despite being hampered and racing in the unfavoured group, in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (finished tenth of 25 overall, fourth of nine on the far side) in latest 6f start; one of the form players, upped in trip.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: Blue Point colt; sibling to two winners, notably Wolf Of Badenoch (Group-placed 7f 2yo/1m3f; RPR 101); dam 12.4f AW/1m5f turf scorer (89), half-sister to Irish Oaks winner Even So; probably one of the better types among the newcomers.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: Zoustar half-brother to 12 winners, notably James Garfield (6f/7f including 2yo Group 2; RPR 119); dam 6f/7f 2yo scorer (103); from a family that his connections know well; the betting may offer further guidance.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: 450,000euros breeze-up 2yo buy who holds two Group entries; hindered his chance with an awkward start and some greenness en route to finishing third of nine (as 4-5 favourite) over 6f at Windsor; recorded a modest RPR but should do better with the experience under his belt.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: Holds a Group 1 entry; has two pieces of experience, namely fourth-place finishes in Naas barrier trial and Leopardstown event (7f, good); shaped particularly well on latter occasion, finishing nicely once seeing daylight; brings potential and adds great interest.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: 30,000euros yearling; Awtaad half-brother to two winners, notably Endless Power (1m/9.4f AW; RPR 95); dam unraced half-sister to Oaks winner Qualify; pitched into a warm maiden on debut; likely best watched.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: Green and in rear throughout at Newmarket, finishing almost 5l behind Al Wathba; may do better with the experience under his belt but has work to do to reverse placings with that rival.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: 38,000euros foal, 70,000gns yearling; Phoenix Of Spain half-brother to Listed-placed 5f/6f 2yo winner Rush Queen (RPR 88); dam unraced, out of maiden half-sister to Group-placed 1m 2yo winner Yaseer; begins career in rather deep waters.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: 45,000gns yearling; by Australia; dam placed at 1m2f/1m3f in Germany, sibling to a few very useful German winners, notably Elle Shadow (triple 1m2f Group 3); probably one to look out for over longer trips later on.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: Has shown ability in 6f contests, finishing fourth both times and earning a mark of 77 which is 3lb below the one allotted to stablemate Rafe's Da Man but this is the first string on jockey arrangements and still open to progress with this new trip a plus on breeding.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Spotlight: Showed promise with second-place finish in 6f event at Chester while shaping as if today's extra furlong will suit; this is a stronger race but he's open to progress and could go well.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
OwnerName: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
Spotlight: Ballydoyle colt who holds several Group entries; unable to quicken in steadily run maiden at the Curragh (7f, good to firm) but stuck on for fourth of six and should be capable of improvement, especially if getting a stronger pace kept to this distance; shortlisted.

Third to Blue Courvoisier in the Silver Bowl at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) in May and bounced back from Royal Ascot defeat (drawn on the wrong side) for clear second at Ascot (1m, good to firm), when a nose behind Ciarrai Abu who followed up here on Thursday; he should stay this far, and this progressive 3yo could be on an advantageous mark up 4lb since last time.

Fifth of 16 in this last year in a race that favoured those ridden more prominently and he's been in career-best form at Sandown on his last two starts, posting a win (1m, good) and a very creditable third of 12 (1m2f, good); could be involved.

Built upon previous promise to win the Silver Bowl at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) in May on his third handicap start; mid-division in the Britannia at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) since when fifth of 15 on the unfavoured far side; this 3yo remains of interest and is firmly in calculations.

4yo who was making his seventh start when winning at Epsom (8.5f, good) in April; two lesser runs have followed but it wasn't a bad effort at Sandown last time and the fact he excelled at Epsom bodes well for today's first visit to Goodwood, which has similarities; wears a first-time tongue-tie.

Inconsistent and his losing sequence is up to 11 races; however, he was a close third off this reduced mark at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) last time and is an each-way contender if backing up that performance.

5yo who won last year on first two starts before good second on handicap debut at Haydock where he was 7lb higher; however, his form has gone the wrong way since and there was no revival on last month's stable debut.

Close third at Newmarket (good) in June on his first crack at 1m and second start for this yard, and he made good headway before his run petered out in the John Smith's Cup at York (10.2f, good to firm), finishing sixth of 22; has won here and today's drop back in trip/grade could prove ideal.

Third of 15 for Richard Hughes in the Golden Mile here last August when 5lb higher; hasn't hit the same heights since, most recently fifth of nine at Redcar when the 6-4 favourite; however, he's on a dangerous mark and is not written off; interesting to see if he's again strong in the betting.

Kept on for second at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) in April and he's run well in fourth on both starts since (1m2f/1m4f, good to soft/good to firm); he's never raced over a trip this short and it isn't an obvious plus, but on the flip-side a well-run race in this big field should play to his strengths.

Two-time French winner who could improve from his British debut at Kempton (1m4f, AW) last month, when fifth of seven; dropped 2lb but there's a suspicion he remains on a tough mark; wears first-time cheekpieces.

9yo who won two in a row at Lingfield (1m2f/1m1f, good to firm) and maybe went off too hard when well beaten at Sandown (1m2f, good) last time; has won here twice and he might not be far away if bouncing back.

Course winner who won two in a row last May (1m, good) and is 4lb below his last winning mark; showed some spark at Meydan in January but hasn't shone in Britain on his two runs since and needs to turn things around.

Extremely well handicapped on his old form; it appeared to bode very well for this campaign when he was runner-up at Sandown in May on his second stable start, but he's failed to kick on and has something to prove.

Seven-time winner in France; this front-runner was runner-up in twice in a row for Tom Dascombe last July/September but things didn't go to plan on his final two runs for that yard (Flat/hurdles) and he was well beaten on his stable and seasonal debut at Chepstow in May.

Ex-Ballydoyle 4yo who has been running for Norwegian yard this year; won in Norway in May but struggled in handicaps at Meydan early this year and was well beaten in the Buckingham Palace at Royal Ascot in June (third of six in far-side group); others are preferred.

RaceName: Scullion Law 'Law Firm For Life' EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in fast-ground maidens at Brighton (5.5f) and Yarmouth (5f) on last two starts; sets a fair standard and shapes as if 6f could suit.

RaceName: Scullion Law 'Law Firm For Life' EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Harry Angel colt who was sent off at 33-1 and finished well held on his Ascot debut three weeks ago.

RaceName: Scullion Law 'Law Firm For Life' EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 140,000gns breeze-up purchase who never threatened when sixth of ten on Newbury debut (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago, but looked to be getting the hang of things late and improvement is very much on cards; Tuesday's Goodwood maiden winner Agrippa was second so it was probably a decent race.

RaceName: Scullion Law 'Law Firm For Life' EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 200,000euros breeze-up purchase out of a mare who failed to win herself but is from a good family; betting informative for stable which enjoys plenty of first-time-out 2yo success.

RaceName: Scullion Law 'Law Firm For Life' EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Space Blues half-brother to 6f/7f AW 2yo winner Ghisa (RPR 77); dam unraced half-sister to some useful sorts; yard had an easy 2yo winner here (although not first time up) in June so a market move would be interesting.

RaceName: Strathmore Hotels Ltd Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Form has been up and down, but one of his better efforts when beaten a neck in a Pontefract maiden (1m2f, good) last month; solid claims granted a similar effort.

RaceName: Strathmore Hotels Ltd Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Overcame greenness when narrowly making a winning debut at Leicester (1m2f, good to soft) last September, but although only beating one home in a Listed contest at Goodwood (1m4f, good) in May, she did meet trouble; respected if resuming her progress.

RaceName: Strathmore Hotels Ltd Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in all three starts this year, the latest behind a nice sort (just beaten in a Goodwood handicap on Wednesday) at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm; first start since being gelded) last month; big shout, especially if the cheekpieces have a positive effect.

RaceName: Strathmore Hotels Ltd Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Not disgraced when fourth of five in a Chester maiden (1m2f, good; 150-1) in May, but he still has a bit to find and looks one for handicaps after this.

RaceName: Strathmore Hotels Ltd Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister to winners Earn Your Stripes (5f/6f; RPR 59) and Willy Il Coyote (Italian 6.7f-1m); dam 1m4f AW winner (58), half-sister to US 8.5f stakes winner Lilbourne Eliza and Listed-placed 1m/1m2f winner Terre Neuve; hooded on debut and wouldn't be an obvious winner first time out; refused to enter the stalls for her intended debut at Carlisle in June.

OwnerName: Hot To Trot Racing 1 And Mrs David Egan
Spotlight: Out of her depth in Listed company at Pontefract (1m4f, good) 15 days ago, but suggested she retains ability after returning from another lengthy absence in March; return to a longer trip may suit and respected down in grade.

2-5 since joining this yard, winning at Pontefract (2m2f, good; first-time visor) in June and over hurdles at Cartmel a fortnight ago; clearly in good heart, but this may not be far enough for him now.

Lightly raced 7yo who won at Musselburgh (2m, good) in May and Ayr (1m7f, soft) in June; however, he seemed to find the trip too sharp over C&D (good) in between and ran poorly over 2m when favourite at Musselburgh on Friday.

Made a successful stable debut/reappearance at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) in April, but a 5lb rise seemed to find her out at York (1m4f, good) the following month; bred to stay this far, but she needs to bounce back after 79 days off.
Six of his eight wins have come over 1m3f/1m4f here and is 6lb lower than for the most recent, but yet to click since returning in May; dual-handed stable won this in 2022 and 2023.
0-8; finished fourth of 15 on her third start for the yard at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm; 50-1) last time, but was still 15l behind the winner; another 2lb drop not enough to tempt.

OwnerName: Hambleton Racing Ltd XXXV & E Burke
Spotlight: Edging back down the weights and now 3lb higher than for the latest of two wins over 1m6f last September; wore cheekpieces in a void race last month, but this is effectively his first start in them; shortlisted.
Three-time winner over 1m3f/1m4f on a soft surface in France, but he hasn't beaten many in five starts for this yard; down another 3lb, but hard to fancy.
Beaten upwards of 10l in three maidens over 7f-1m4f; from a highly successful staying family and worth a market check on handicap debut.

Made all on his final start for Ross Burdon at Yarmouth (11.5f, soft) in June, since when he changed hands for 19,000gns; 4lb rise fair enough, but he could do with some rain; one of two runners for yard that took this in 2024.

Won 5f handicaps at Haydock (good) and here (soft) on his first two runs for Ed Bethell last September; has recorded even better form in defeat this year, notably his close second of 14 in the Gosforth Park Cup (5f) five weeks ago; won't be inconvenienced should any of the forecast showers arrive; gets the vote.
Won last season's Portland handicap at Doncaster (good) off a 2lb higher mark; looked on the way back when runner-up back at Doncaster early last month but two lesser runs have followed.

Largely progressive form; ran a cracker on what was effectively her seasonal return (unseated her rider soon after start on reappearance) when fourth of 15 in 5f Ayr Listed race (soft) in June; travelled strongly close to the pace in 6f York Group 3 (good to firm) since and the return to 5f could suit back in handicap company; part of a strong hand for Ed Bethell.

OwnerName: M McHale, J Munroe, M Guy & D Walshe
Spotlight: Four wins last season, including C&D on good; 0-6 in 2026 but latest Southwell third creditable and he's back on a winning mark.
Back in form since fitted with blinkers, scoring over C&D (good) in May; has reached the frame on all three outings since, although latest fourth of seven at Pontefract was no more than respectable.
He is a better horse on AW than turf; a much lower mark in this sphere reflects that but his 1-28 record on the grass doesn't mark him down as the likely winner of this.
Landed a 5f Bahrain handicap in January but has struggled since; the handicapper is starting to relent but others are still preferred.

He hasn't won since a Listed success at York (6f, soft) in October 2023, but he's started for Robert Cowell with a trio of creditable efforts in competitive handicaps; could click for this yard at some point.
Below par in three AW outings this year and a return to turf and first-time blinkers failed to spark a revival at Beverley in April; absent since (has had wind surgery for a second time).

Running well this year, including close third to Vantheman over C&D in May, and he posted a deserved win in a big field at Ayr (6f, good) 26 days ago; raised 5lb but he was very competitive off similar marks in 2024.

Made it 3-5 since joining Mick Appleby when seeing off 19 rivals in the Epsom Dash (5f, good to soft) eight weeks ago; had the advantage of racing against the near rail but most of his 6lb rise is offset by the promising Conor Whiteley's claim.

OwnerName: N Irving, F Steele & I Jardine
Spotlight: Made it 3-10 on the AW when successful at Newcastle last month; up 5lb and 1-13 on turf, but a stiff 5f seems to suit her well; looks the pick of the stable's trio.

Another who has a better strike-rate on AW (7-19) than on turf (1-17); patchy form so far this year, but has dropped 3lb below his last winning mark and this is a drop in class; stable also runs Thunderstorm Katie.

Has been consistent since his successful reappearance at Southwell (6f, AW) in January and was only beaten 2l into fourth of eight in a 0-85 at Beverley last month; suited by a stiff 5f and much respected down in class.
Back off the same mark as when winning at Carlisle (5f, good) in May, but not very consistent so not quite sure what to expect.
Has a better strike-rate on the AW (4-26) than on turf (3-39); 4lb below his last winning mark, but has to put a modest effort at Ayr (5f, good to firm) last month behind him.
1lb below his last winning mark but usually misses the break and has finished out of the frame in all five starts this year; rain would help.
Losing run up to 16, but has won twice over C&D and ran better than it looked when sixth of 11 at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) 11 days ago; 20lb below his last winning mark and could go well at a price.
1lb below his last winning mark, but is another who would have made more appeal on the AW (5-10) than turf (1-40).

One of five wins in the second half of last season was over C&D in August; four seconds (including over 5f/6f here) from the back in her last five starts this term, back to form at Musselburgh last night; each-way claims.

Holds her form really well despite being kept busy, winning three times here since mid-June and making it 12 course wins overall; the return here is a big plus, but all 14 career wins have come over 6f so she does have something to prove on a rare attempt at 5f; stable also runs Harb.
2-5 over C&D, the latest win coming in first-time cheekpieces in June (good to firm, has won on soft); still just 2lb higher, but not the most consistent; first-time blinkers.

OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing Lxvi And P Demilow
Spotlight: Low-mileage 3yo whose form since handicapping features a reappearance win at Redcar (1m) in April and keeping-on second at Carlisle (1m1f, good to soft) in June; beaten by more than lack of stamina over 1m2f at Pontefract since, though.

OwnerName: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd
Spotlight: Progressive 4yo who scored over C&D (good to soft) in June before making it five wins in his last seven starts when overcoming interference to shade a close finish at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) four weeks ago; he and the second were clear of the rest on Town Moor so a 4lb rise may not stop him.

Hold-up performer who is thrown in on his 2025 form but has yet to really get going this time round, including beaten 5l when third of six at Ayr (7f) 12 days ago; Paul Mulrennan, who has been on board for eight of his ten wins, is on Sanafi Zabeel this time.
Ex-German 1m1f winner; gained a first win for current yard over C&D (good to firm) in May and has matched that form when third here on his last two starts; likely to be on the premises again.

Had been bubbling under prior to winning easily at Redcar (1m, good to firm) last month; keeping on (although still had a fair bit of ground to make up) when clipping heels and coming down 1f out at York last Saturday; 9lb higher than at Redcar but still a potential class act at this level if that nasty experience last weekend hasn't left a mark.

OwnerName: David Orr & Miss L A Perratt
Spotlight: Course winner who added to his tally at Ayr (1m, good to firm) in May; good runner-up efforts there in recent weeks and has to enter calculations.

Cost 550,000euros as a 2yo but has yet to make a significant impact, including last of six on 7.5f Beverley handicap debut (good) 39 days ago; much too soon to write him off for leading stable but first-time cheekpieces need to give him a lift.

OwnerName: Future Champions Racing Syn & Ben Haslam
Spotlight: Won his final start in Ireland (1m, heavy); hasn't been in the same form for new stable but worth a second look in the betting back from a two-month break.
Good and bad in six runs for this yard, failing to build on a decent run at Newcastle when seventh of eight at Doncaster last time.

Landed 6f Ascot novice (soft) for Hugo Palmer last September; little to shout about since but his mark has tumbled as a result and Adam Nicol does well with new recruits (same owners); one to keep an eye on in the betting.

Bids for a hat-trick after two wins on good to firm ground at Redcar, the latest in an apprentice handicap over 1m under Conor Whiteley on Wednesday; can race off 1lb lower and shouldn't have an issue with stepping back up trip, while rain would also be no problem; major claims.
All four wins have come on the AW at Chelmsford (7f-1m2f) and is 0-11 on turf; plenty to prove on his return from ten months off with cheekpieces given a go.
Has twice made the frame over 6f this year, but 0-13 and has plenty to prove on this first attempt beyond 7f.

Mainly campaigned over shorter but does stay this far; 399 days off before this season; never-never fourth of seven at Musselburgh (7f) last night was probably his most positive display since; back on his last winning mark.

Dual winner over the extended 1m here; losing run up to 13, but 16lb below her last winning mark and looked unlucky not to finish closer when fourth of six here (1m, good) three weeks ago; stays this far and could go well.
Back off the same mark as for his successful Nottingham reappearance (1m, good) in April, but his form has regressed since; enough to prove.
5-37 on the AW but 0-24 on turf; hasn't looked like exploiting his declining mark of late; visor returns.
Made it 15th-time lucky at Newcastle (1m, AW) a week ago; now needs to show he can do it back on turf from 4lb higher and also still has stamina to prove.

RaceName: Professional Horse Racing Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Well-bred filly who won small-field C&D (good) maiden in May, her second start, and was creditable second on handicap debut at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) last month; still has more improvement to come; good chance.

RaceName: Professional Horse Racing Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won off today's mark on Polytrack here (1m2f) in April; not quite at same level on turf since but was persistently denied clear run when fourth of six at Sandown (1m2f, good to firm; behind Percival) nine days ago and has possibilities if his luck improves.

RaceName: Professional Horse Racing Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Yet to add to his Group 3 win at Glorious Goodwood three years ago but placed several times this year, losing out only by a neck at Epsom (1m4f, good to firm) on latest outing 16 days ago; remains on a workable mark and will be fine over today's shorter trip; probably on the premises again.

RaceName: Professional Horse Racing Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Lightly raced since heavy-ground win on debut in France in November 2024 but bettered low-key stable debut when respectable third at Sandown (1m2f, good to firm; hood removed) nine days ago, despite racing too freely; any further progress here will make him a serious player.

RaceName: Professional Horse Racing Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2-3 as a 2yo; not much has gone to plan on his two starts this year but he had soft ground as a plausible excuse for 56l defeat at Epsom (1m2f) on Derby Derby, and his down-the-field finish at Ascot (1m; first-time hood) last month came in a warm 3yo handicap; this race is easier and it would be dangerous to write him off at this stage.

RaceName: Happy 50th Birthday Joanne Baker Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-16 but made brave bold from the front before weakening into third at Epsom (1m4f, good) last month and faced impossible task when second of four behind well-handicapped rival here (1m6f, good to firm) a week ago; ought to be suited by this drop back in trip; dangerous if allowed to dominate.

RaceName: Happy 50th Birthday Joanne Baker Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 13-race maiden; placed in two AW handicaps in early part of this year (1m/9.4f) but beaten about 16l when fourth of five on turf return at Windsor (1m, good to firm) in June; must do better here.

RaceName: Happy 50th Birthday Joanne Baker Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Kept on for third in AW handicap here (1m2f) in March but was well down the field on both subsequent starts (1m4f/1m2f) and is now 0-9; eased in grade but needs three-month break to have done her good.

RaceName: Happy 50th Birthday Joanne Baker Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Lightly raced after only five starts and wasn't disgraced when fifth of seven in this grade at Yarmouth (11.5f, good to firm) last month but needs to take another step forward.

RaceName: Happy 50th Birthday Joanne Baker Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Below form in 1m2f Yarmouth handicap last month (no headgear) but returned to the Flat with win in refitted cheekpieces (back on today) over that C&D (good to firm) in June and has strong claims if back at that level.

RaceName: Happy 50th Birthday Joanne Baker Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Yet to show any worthwhile form after six starts, the penultimate over C&D in this grade; significant improvement required.

Much improved since hiked up in trip and switched to handicaps this season, and bids to complete a hat-trick after small-field success in first-time cheekpieces at Newbury (2m, good to firm) nine days ago; has an ungainly head carriage but is probably still well treated after latest 4lb rise.

Clear second to fast-improving rival over C&D (good) on latest Flat start in June and also ran well over hurdles last month; may not have much margin for error off current mark but can make his presence felt.
Won three in a row in a visor this spring (1m6f-2m1f, good to firm/good) but recent efforts suggest the handicapper may have her measure now; tried in blinkers here; needs to kick on again.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a Listed-placed German winner; showed inexperience in early stages but ran on well for clear second of five (no threat to winner) on last month's debut at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm); ought to be more streetwise here; leading contender.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a half-sister to Group-placed 6f/7f 2yo winner Gavota; made quite promising debut when keeping-on third of ten at Kempton (6f, AW) in December; gelded during subsequent eight-month break and has tongue-tie fitted for turf debut; shortlisted.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Displayed promise on first three starts, most notably when third over C&D (good) in May; has a bit to find on the figures with a couple of these but can collect another minor prize; hooded for first time.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Struggled (albeit on soft ground) on debut here (7.6f) in June and didn't achieve much when last of five at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) last month; difficult to enthuse over.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beaten over 15l when last of five on last month's debut at Ripon (1m, good); not the most obvious answer here.
Built upon encouraging debut when third of ten in Newbury novice (6f, good to firm) last month, despite racing too freely, and should have more improvement to come in nurseries; must be considered.
Creditable third behind two useful rivals in valuable C&D (good) novice in June and had excuse when well beaten on latest outing (struck into); needs to be taken very seriously on nursery debut.

Safely held when sixth of seven on last month's nursery debut at Nottingham but subsequent seventh of 24 in Newbury's Super Sprint (also 5f, good to firm; first-time hood) was commendable, particularly as she was first of seven home in the far-side group; can feature if suited by this new trip.
Won here when dropped back to 5f (good to firm) for recent nursery debut; could quite plausibly have more to offer back at 6f but is 5lb higher in a higher-grade race today.
Scored over C&D (good to firm) on nursery debut 17 days ago, beating the warm favourite; could still be well treated after recent 3lb rise; obvious contender.

Behind Seed Ya Later when tenth of 24 in Newbury's Super Sprint (5f, good to firm) a fortnight ago and has now been unplaced all four starts; needs combination of new trip and first-time cheekpieces to unlock improvement on this nursery debut.
Only beaten about 2l when fifth of six on recent nursery debut at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) and is 2lb lower here but others have stronger claims.

Close second twice on good to firm turf last month before winning in first-time cheekpieces on Tapeta (also 7f) 11 days ago; 5lb higher here but commands respect in current form; usual tongue-tie (left off last time) is refitted.
Came good at 11th attempt, with clearcut win from off the pace in C&D (good to firm) classified ten days ago; has more on her plate in this handicap but further progress is possible.

Has modest 2-39 strike-rate, with both wins gained on AW, and tends to race too freely but the form of his never-dangerous fourth at Brighton (7f, good to firm) at end of June has worked out well; worth a second look.
Led close home for narrow AW win here in January but that's his only success from 21 starts and he posed no threat on turf at Brighton last month; others have more pressing claims.

Soundly beaten on all three turf starts, most recently in soft-ground C&D contest won by Beau Jardine in early June, but now 1lb lower than when winning on Polytrack here in December and has possibilities if this fast ground suits.
Ended long losing run with soft-ground C&D win in June and gave another good account when fourth at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) 11 days ago; probably won't be far away.
Still unexposed after only five starts but raced too freely and was soundly beaten on handicap debut at Kempton (7f, AW) in February; returns from five-month break.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Began season with two decent efforts over 1m before justifying skinny odds in tactical, four-runner contest at Ffos Las (7.3f, good) on Tuesday; effectively only 4lb higher under 5lb penalty here, and evidently in good nick.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Kept on well to score at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) last month and is now 2-7; still unexposed on turf and promises to be suited by today's slightly longer trip; ought to be right in the thick of things.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Useful 2yo who needed significant help from the handicapper before her narrow win in first-time visor here (7f, good to firm; made all) ten days ago; went back up only 2lb for that, though; respected.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won her first two races; disappointing when favourite for Lingfield Oaks Trial in the spring but firmly back on track when second in French Listed event (1m4f, good; collared late on after being clear over 1f out) six weeks ago; still has untapped potential.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Useful on her day; highly tried and not at best so far this year, but she ran respectably when never-nearer fourth of eight in Irish Group 3 (1m2f, good to firm) two weeks ago; moves into unknown territory trip-wise but her pedigree gives hope that she'll stay and this is a drop in grade.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: From a family that has served these connections well; 0-10 since her debut success but she finished close behind Orionis when fifth in C&D Listed race (7-4 favourite) last time; previous two efforts read even better and she's a major player with a visor replacing cheekpieces.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Sea The Stars half-sister to the same connections' Oaks winner Soul Sister; arrives on an upward curve after easy novice win at Lingfield and unlucky second in handicap at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm; stayed on well after being short of room); plenty to find on bare form in this higher grade but she should be well suited by this step up in trip and cannot be discounted.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Reliable type whose wins have come in 1m2f and 1m6f handicaps; good fourth on her only attempts at Listed company but she'll need a personal best if she's to make a winning reappearance after ten months off.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Best effort when winning Goodwood handicap (1m4f, good) in May; respectable third in C&D Listed race two weeks ago, racing freely and finding no extra; may not have reached her ceiling just yet and she's high on the list.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Listed winner and Group 3 runner-up for the Gosdens last year; has shown she retains all her ability, fourth in Group 2 over C&D (good to firm; wore tongue-strap) last month; this is easier and she should be thereabouts in a first-time hood.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Has improved with each run this year, winning maiden at Ripon (1m3f, good) and handicap at Salisbury (1m4f, good to firm; dug deep to see off main challenger by a neck), both in small fields; this is a sterner assignment but she's still unexposed and in good hands.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Green on debut but hasn't looked back since and she forced a dead-heat in C&D Listed race (good to firm; 100-30) last time; may have more in the tank and she's high on the list once more.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
